# Component library

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-components.mjs from each file's @motomation-component header. Do not edit by hand. -->

43 components across 6 families, written for this skill. Each is one file, typed in strict TypeScript, React only, with no other dependencies. They share a small helper file (`_lib/motion.ts`) for reduced motion, pointer type, viewport and scroll progress. Every component has props with sensible defaults, a reduced-motion path, a touch behaviour, and notes on when it earns its place and when it's slop.

**Use them like this:** a component is a starting point for a concept, not a finished design. Pick one because the Thinking Sequence asked for it, tune its props to the brief, and keep it inside the tier budget. The signature move is designed for the brief. If a component here matches it, bend the component to the concept rather than the other way round.

**Install one into a project:**

```bash
# copy the file plus _lib/motion.ts into your components folder, or use the registry:
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design/main/registry/<id>.json
```

**See them live:** open `examples/gallery/index.html` in a browser (self-contained, no build). Toggle reduced motion in your OS to see every fallback.

## Type

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`BlurFocus`](type/blur-focus.tsx) | 2 | Words sharpen from a soft blur into focus, one after another, as the line enters the screen. | The concept is about clarity, focus, eyesight, photography or waking up. | Every heading on the page; long paragraphs; low-end devices with many instances. | Text is sharp and visible from the start. |
| [`CurvedText`](type/curved-text.tsx) | 1 | Text set around a circle like a stamp or seal, with an optional slow turn. | Badges, stamps, seals, "since" marks and a single rotating label beside a primary action. | Anything the reader must read quickly; as a loading spinner; more than one per screen. | The ring is still. |
| [`Decode`](type/decode.tsx) · signature `decode` | 2 | A short label resolves from random glyphs, left to right, when it enters the screen or on hover. | Technical, secret or data-led brands; labels of 1–4 words. | Body text, headlines longer than a line, or more than one per screen. | Shows the final text at once; no glyph cycling. |
| [`InkFill`](type/ink-fill.tsx) · signature `ink-fill` | 2 | A statement starts in the muted colour and fills with ink word by word as the reader scrolls through it. | Manifestos, about statements, a single paragraph that is the page's idea. | More than one per page; text the reader needs before scrolling (it must stay readable when muted). | The whole statement is in ink from the start. |
| [`LetterRelay`](type/letter-relay.tsx) · signature `letter-relay` | 2 | A large hero name shrinks and travels into a fixed header slot letter by letter as you scroll the first screen, so the name hands itself to the navigation. | Portfolios and personal brands where the name is the identity. | Long names (over ~16 characters); pages without a fixed header; product pages. | The hero name and the header name are both static; no scroll listener runs. |
| [`NeighbourMoves`](type/neighbour-moves.tsx) · signature `neighbour-moves` | 2 | Each letter of a name has its own small move on hover (lift, tilt, stretch, spin, drop), so the word feels like a cast of characters. | Personal names, studio names and play-mood logotypes of 3–12 letters. | Navigation, body text, or brands that must feel calm. | No hover moves. |
| [`PressureType`](type/pressure-type.tsx) | 2 | Each letter of one display word stretches wider and heavier as the cursor nears it, like pressing into rubber. | Playful, elastic or physical brands with a variable font that has wdth and wght axes. | Fonts without variable axes; more than one word; any body copy. | Letters stay at the base width and weight. |
| [`ScrollFloat`](type/scroll-float.tsx) | 2 | Letters of a display line rise and settle into place one by one, driven by scroll position, so scrolling back reverses it. | Play-mood display lines that should feel buoyant; one line per section. | Serious or institutional briefs; text that must be readable before it settles (prices, dates). | Letters sit in place; no scroll listener runs. |
| [`SplitFlap`](type/split-flap.tsx) | 2 | Each character flips through the alphabet to its value like a departure board, settling left to right; changing the value flips again. | Schedules, line-ups, menus, travel, times and short codes. | Long text; values the reader must trust mid-animation (the final value is announced, not the flips). | Shows the new value at once. |
| [`WidthSprint`](type/width-sprint.tsx) · signature `width-sprint` | 2 | A display word stretches wider the faster you scroll and relaxes back when you stop, using the font's width axis. | Sport, speed, events and launches with a variable font that has a wdth axis. | Fonts without wdth; more than one element; layouts where the word could overflow at its widest. | The word stays at its base width. |

## Scroll

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`Aperture`](scroll/aperture.tsx) · signature `aperture` | 2 | The next section opens through a growing circle (an iris) as you scroll into it, from a small porthole to full bleed. | A chapter change that is a real threshold: entering a room, a lens, a window, a reveal of the product. | Every section; content that must be readable at the edges before the iris opens. | The section is fully open from the start. |
| [`DarkroomDevelop`](scroll/darkroom-develop.tsx) · signature `darkroom-develop` | 2 | A photograph develops from blank paper as it scrolls in: pale and flat first, then contrast, then tone, like a print in the tray. | Photography, archives, memory, analogue brands; one image per screen. | Product shots the buyer must inspect; galleries of many small images. | The photo is fully developed from the start. |
| [`HorizontalReel`](scroll/horizontal-reel.tsx) · signature `horizontal-reel` | 2 | A section pins and vertical scroll pulls a strip of frames sideways, like film through a gate; a frame counter follows. | Film, gallery, timeline and process concepts with 4–10 frames. | Content people need to scan quickly; more than one per page; frames that need reading time. | The frames become a normal horizontally scrollable row with snap points. |
| [`ReadingRail`](scroll/reading-rail.tsx) | 1 | A thin rail at the top or edge of the screen fills as you read an article, with an optional chapter label that changes at each heading. | Long reads, case studies and documentation pages. | Short pages; landing pages; next to another progress indicator. | The rail still reflects progress (it's information, not decoration) but moves in 5% steps instead of continuously. |
| [`StackedDeck`](scroll/stacked-deck.tsx) · signature `stacked-deck` | 2 | Cards stick one after another and stack like a deck; covered cards step back and dim, leaving their titles as a table of contents. | Sequences, case studies, steps and services with 3–6 items. | More than 6 cards; cards taller than the viewport; content that must be compared side by side. | Cards stack with sticky positioning but don't scale or dim. |
| [`Thread`](scroll/thread.tsx) · signature `thread` | 2 | One line draws itself down the page as you scroll, linking sections like a seam, a route or a timeline. | Journeys, timelines, craft (stitching, drawing), routes and process pages. | As decoration on a page without a journey; together with another scroll signature. | The line is fully drawn and still. |
| [`VelocityMarquee`](scroll/velocity-marquee.tsx) | 2 | A looping marquee that drifts on its own, speeds up with scroll speed, follows scroll direction and leans (skews) while you scroll fast. | Sport, launches, events and a single line of brand words between sections. | Content the reader needs (prices, dates); more than one marquee per page. | A static, wrapped row of the same words. |

## Cursor

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`ImageTrail`](cursor/image-trail.tsx) | 2 | Moving the cursor across an area drops a trail of images that appear, linger briefly and shrink away, cycling through a set. | Photographers, archives, studios with a deep body of work; one area per page. | Fewer than 5 images; e-commerce product pages; over text that must be read. | The images are shown as a static row instead. |
| [`Lens`](cursor/lens.tsx) · signature `lens` | 2 | A circle follows the cursor and reveals a second layer underneath: sketch under final, night under day, before under after. | The two layers are the story (process, transformation, hidden detail). | The second layer is decoration; text-heavy layers; more than one per page. | The lens jumps to the cursor without easing; a "Show the other layer" toggle shows the second layer at full size. |
| [`PixelWake`](cursor/pixel-wake.tsx) · signature `pixel-wake` | 2 | The cursor leaves a trail of square pixels on a grid that fade out behind it, like a wake on a low-resolution screen. | Digital, pixel, retro, game and screen-themed concepts; usually only over the hero. | Over body text; on calm or luxury briefs; together with another cursor effect. | No trail. |
| [`SeismographLine`](cursor/seismograph-line.tsx) · signature `seismograph-line` | 2 | A hairline divider bends toward the cursor as it passes and springs back with a small wobble, like a needle on a seismograph. | Dividers on calm editorial pages where one living detail is enough; sound, measurement and science brands. | Every divider; busy pages; pages that already have a cursor effect. | A straight line. |
| [`TargetCursor`](cursor/target-cursor.tsx) | 2 | A small crosshair follows the cursor; over anything clickable it snaps out into corner brackets that frame the target. | Precision tools, cameras, games, architecture and engineering concepts. | Content sites; together with another cursor effect; when it would hide the system cursor (it doesn't by default). | Brackets jump to targets without easing. |
| [`TiltCard`](cursor/tilt-card.tsx) | 2 | A card rotates in 3D toward the cursor with a soft moving highlight, like holding a physical card to the light. | Physical objects: tickets, cards, passes, packaging, a single product. | Grids of many cards; text-heavy cards; cards that are links to long content (the motion distracts). | Flat card, no rotation or highlight. |

## Backgrounds

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`ContourLines`](backgrounds/contour-lines.tsx) | 2 | Topographic contour lines drawn as SVG that slowly drift, like a map breathing; deterministic from a seed. | Landscape, outdoors, climate, geography, agriculture and mapping concepts. | Urban or tech brands without a land story; behind dense text. | Still lines. |
| [`DotField`](backgrounds/dot-field.tsx) | 2 | A grid of dots that swell and push away from the cursor, then ease back, like a pin-art board. | Technical, structural, data or grid-led concepts; behind a hero with little text. | Behind body text; organic or luxury briefs; together with a cursor signature. | A still dot grid. |
| [`Grain`](backgrounds/grain.tsx) | 1 | A film-grain layer over a section or the whole page, static by default or gently flickering at a low frame rate. | Analogue, photographic, warm or printed moods; to take the digital edge off flat colour. | Over small text at high opacity; on clinical, technical brands; animated on low-end mobile. | Static grain. |
| [`Halftone`](backgrounds/halftone.tsx) | 2 | Renders an image as print dots on a canvas, sized by brightness, like a newspaper photo; dots can grow in as it enters the screen. | Print, newspaper, zine, poster, protest and retro concepts. | Product photos people must inspect; portraits where likeness matters; many on one page. | Dots render at full size immediately. |
| [`LightSweep`](backgrounds/light-sweep.tsx) | 1 | A slow band of light crosses a surface every few seconds, like sun moving through a window or a scanner pass. | Architecture, light, time-of-day and hospitality concepts; behind one hero or one card. | Behind text where the band would drop contrast; as a "shimmer" on buttons; more than one per screen. | No sweep. |
| [`LiquidField`](backgrounds/liquid-field.tsx) | 4 | Slow flowing colour like ink in water or silk in wind, drawn by a tiny WebGL fragment shader with a CSS gradient fallback. | The material really is liquid, fabric, light or weather; behind a hero with one line of type. | As generic "AI gradient" decoration; behind body text; on pages that already use WebGL. | A still frame of the same colours. |

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`BentoReveal`](layout/bento-reveal.tsx) | 1 | A modular grid of mixed-size tiles that enter in reading order with a short stagger the first time the grid scrolls in. | Content that truly has mixed weights (one big feature, several small facts). | Equal-weight content (use a list); as the default landing layout (it's overused); more than one per page. | Tiles are visible from the start. |
| [`CurveCarousel`](layout/curve-carousel.tsx) | 2 | Cards sit on a shallow arc; the focused card is upright and in front, its neighbours tilt and recede. Arrow keys, buttons, drag and swipe move it. | 3–9 case studies or products where one at a time is the point. | Content people need to compare; more than 9 items; as autoplaying decoration. | Cards change position without easing. |
| [`Dock`](layout/dock.tsx) | 2 | A row of icon buttons that magnify smoothly as the cursor passes along them, neighbours growing a little less. | App-like tool collections, launchers and playful personal sites with 4–8 actions. | Primary navigation that needs labels; touch-first sites; more than 8 items. | No magnification. |
| [`FlowingMenu`](layout/flowing-menu.tsx) | 2 | A big typographic list of links; hovering an item rolls a band over it from the edge the cursor entered, carrying a marquee of the item's words. | Portfolio and studio navigation or project indexes with 3–8 entries. | Primary site navigation on product sites; long lists; touch-first audiences. | Hover shows the band instantly with still text. |
| [`InfiniteCanvas`](layout/infinite-canvas.tsx) | 2 | Drag (or use arrow keys) to pan an endless wall of tiles that repeats in every direction, with a little momentum when you let go. | The Gallery Wall archetype: archives, mood boards, studios with lots of visual work. | Fewer than ~12 tiles; content that needs order; as the only way to reach the work (also provide a list). | No momentum; panning still works. |
| [`StickyIndex`](layout/sticky-index.tsx) | 1 | A sticky side index lists the page's sections and highlights the one you are reading, with a marker that slides between entries. | Long case studies, reports, documentation, annual reviews. | Short pages; mobile (it collapses to a top select); landing pages. | The marker jumps instead of sliding. |

## Micro-interactions

| Component | Tier | What it does | Use when | Avoid when | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`BrandSelection`](micro/brand-selection.tsx) · signature `brand-selection` | 1 | Text selection uses the brand accent and ink instead of the browser's blue, scoped to a section or the whole page. | Almost always; it's a tiny, free detail that shows care. | The accent and its text colour don't pass 4.5:1 together. | Not applicable (no motion). |
| [`ClickSpark`](micro/click-spark.tsx) | 1 | A tiny burst of lines radiates from the click point inside a wrapped area, then disappears. | Playful brands, games, and one celebratory action (a like, a ticket added). | Every click on the page; serious briefs; forms. | No spark. |
| [`CopyButton`](micro/copy-button.tsx) | 1 | A copy button whose icon morphs to a tick and whose label says "Copied" for two seconds, then returns. | Install commands, email addresses, codes and coupon strings. | Content the user should read rather than paste. | The tick swaps in without the morph. |
| [`CountUp`](micro/count-up.tsx) | 2 | A number counts from a start value to its real value once, when it first enters the screen, with tabular figures so it doesn't jitter. | Real, sourced figures that are the point of a section (one to three per page). | Invented or rounded-up stats; prices; anything a screenshot mid-count would misreport (see the v2 benchmark note). | Shows the final value at once. |
| [`HoldToCommit`](micro/hold-to-commit.tsx) · signature `hold-to-commit` | 2 | An important action fills while you press and hold, and only confirms when the fill completes; letting go early drains it back. | Irreversible or weighty actions: delete, publish, donate, sign. | Everyday actions; anything time-critical; as the only way to confirm (keyboard users get Enter-to-hold too). | The fill still shows progress (it's information) but with a linear, unanimated drain. |
| [`RememberedList`](micro/remembered-list.tsx) · signature `remembered-list` | 1 | A list of links quietly marks the ones you've already opened (a small tick and a lighter weight), remembered across visits on this device. | Project lists, article archives, course modules, menus people browse more than once. | Lists that change identity often; sensitive topics where "visited" is private information on shared devices. | The mark appears without a transition. |
| [`SquishSwitch`](micro/squish-switch.tsx) | 1 | A toggle whose knob stretches while pressed and squashes as it lands on the other side, like a soft rubber key. | Play-mood products and settings panels where a little character is welcome. | Serious financial or medical settings; dense settings tables. | The knob moves without stretching. |
| [`StickerScatter`](micro/sticker-scatter.tsx) · signature `sticker-scatter` | 2 | Clicking the logo or name bursts a handful of on-brand stickers (emoji or short glyphs) that fly out, spin, land and fade, like emptying a pocket of stickers. | Play-mood personal sites, festivals, kids' brands and events; the logo only. | Serious or institutional briefs; buttons that do something else; repeated clicks on every page element. | Stickers appear around the logo and fade without flying or spinning. |

## Anatomy of a component

Every file starts with the same header, which this catalogue, `data/components.csv` and the registry are generated from. `check-repo` fails if a field is missing or the catalogue is stale.

```tsx
"use client";
// @motomation-component
// id: …
// name: …
// family: …
// tier: …
// deps: …
// what: …
// use-when: …
// avoid-when: …
// reduced-motion: …
// touch: …
// a11y: …
```

Rules for new components: one exported function component, props with defaults, no dependency beyond React unless the tier needs it, a reduced-motion path in code, cleanup of every listener and frame loop, decorative layers `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events: none`, and original code only.
